Let

\[
B_{p,s}=\bigl(d_s(i,j)^p-d_s(i,\ast)^p-d_s(\ast,j)^p\bigr)_{i,j\in Y\setminus\{\ast\}} .
\]

Then \((Y,d_s)\) has \(p\)-negative type exactly when \(B_{p,s}\) is negative semidefinite.

For small \(s>0\), the only distances changing to third order are

\[
d_s(a_1,a_3),\quad d_s(b_1,b_3),\quad d_s(a_2,b_2),
\]

with the lengths given in the statement; all other shortest paths remain the original cycle-path distances.

At \(s=0,p=2\), the restricted matrix \(B_{2,0}\) is negative semidefinite with one-dimensional kernel generated by

\[
(0,1,0,0,1,0),
\]

corresponding to coefficients

\[
c_\ast=-2,\qquad c_{a_2}=c_{b_2}=1,
\]

all others \(0\). The other five eigenvalues are strictly negative, so for small \(s>0\) the endpoint \(\wp(s)\) is the unique nearby zero of the analytic kernel branch.

Writing

\[
\wp(s)=2+A s+B s^2+C s^3+O(s^4),
\]

Taylor expansion of \(\det B_{\wp(s),s}=0\) gives

\[
A=4-\frac{6\log(3/2)}{\log 2},
\]

\[
B=-1.1754671848359985\ldots,
\]

\[
C=1.618068937053428\ldots.
\]

Therefore

\[
\wp(0)=2,
\]

\[
\wp'(0^+)=A=4-\frac{6\log(3/2)}{\log2}
=0.490224995673061\ldots,
\]

\[
\wp''(0^+)=2B=-2.350934369671997\ldots,
\]

\[
\wp'''(0^+)=6C=9.70841362232057\ldots.
\]

Thus the requested tuple is

\[
\boxed{\left(2,\ 0.490224995673061\ldots,\ -2.350934369671997\ldots,\ 9.70841362232057\ldots\right)}.
\]
